title: Add control-plane DB backup (snapshot + verify) and wire into upgrade flow
author: Devon Price
description: This PR introduces a first-class backup step for Redwood Private upgrades that snapshots the control-plane database, verifies the snapshot, and wires the step into the upgrade orchestration. The backup runs before any component upgrades are applied; if the backup or verification fails, the upgrade is aborted and the installer emits a structured failure result with remediation hints. If an upgrade fails after applying chart changes, the installer now triggers the rollback pathway and (when safe) offers to restore the verified pre-upgrade DB snapshot as part of rollback. The implementation is provider-agnostic at the interface level ("snapshotter" + "verifier"), with an initial implementation for Postgres running in-cluster (pg_dump + upload to the configured object store) and verification performed by downloading the artifact and running a deterministic sanity check (dump header + schema introspection) without requiring a full restore into the live DB. Configuration is via installer config/env and CLI flags: --backup-db (default on for upgrade), --skip-backup-db, --backup-retention, and --backup-prefix; all emitted into the upgrade plan output. This also adds metrics/log events around backup duration and artifact size, and extends the upgrade summary output so Support can quickly confirm whether a given upgrade had a verified snapshot. Docs: updated the upgrade README section to clarify required permissions (object store write + read), expected duration, and how to locate the snapshot URI for a restore drill. Testing: unit tests for naming/retention and a lightweight integration test that runs a Postgres container, performs a dump, and validates verification output. Follow-ups: PV snapshots and full restore drills are tracked in ENG-2317 subtask notes; on-prem offline bundle storage is out of scope for this PR.
commits: installer/upgrade: introduce BackupStep interface and wire into step graph
backup/postgres: implement pg_dump snapshotter with object-store uploader
backup/verify: add verifier that downloads artifact and runs sanity checks
upgrade: abort upgrade early on backup failure; surface remediation hints
rollback: plumb snapshot metadata into rollback context; prompt for restore when available
telemetry: emit step timings + artifact size; add structured log fields
tests: add unit tests + docker-based integration test for snapshot/verify
docs: upgrade guide updates (permissions, flags, snapshot location)
changed_files: cmd/redwood-private-installer/upgrade.go (wire BackupStep into upgrade flow; flags/plan output)
internal/upgrade/graph.go (new node type + ordering invariant: backup must complete before apply)
internal/backup/verify/verify.go (download + sanity checks; deterministic exit codes)
internal/ui/summary.go (upgrade summary includes snapshot status + URI)
conversation: Connor O'Brien (review): Can we make backup failure a hard gate (no partial apply) and ensure the step graph enforces this? Also please ensure the snapshot metadata is recorded in the run summary for Support.

Devon Price (author): Yep. BackupStep is inserted before ApplyCharts with a hard dependency edge; upgrade exits before any helm operations if backup/verify fails. Added snapshot URI + verification status to summary output and to the JSON report.

Ethan Park (review): Verification: I’m worried a schema introspection check isn’t enough. Can we at least validate dump integrity (header/version) and that we can list the expected database objects? Also, the verifier must not require DB credentials beyond what the snapshotter already has.

Devon Price (author): Updated verifier to validate pg_dump custom format header + version, then run pg_restore --list (no DB connection) and validate presence of critical schemas/tables (control_plane.*, migrations metadata). No additional DB creds needed.
Sean Gallagher (review): Timeout/retry defaults: object store uploads can be slow; please add bounded retries and log the object size/duration. Also, make sure we don’t leak credentials in logs.

Devon Price (author): Added retry policy (exp backoff, max 6 attempts), explicit 30m upper bound for snapshot with progress logs (bytes transferred). Scrubbed object store URLs to remove query params and ensured env var names are printed, not values.

Marcus Lin (review): Security: confirm snapshot is encrypted at rest (customer-managed if supported) and that access is least-privilege. Also: where is the snapshot URI stored, and is it written to disk?

Devon Price (author): Snapshot is stored in the customer-configured bucket; we don’t change their encryption posture but we document required SSE settings (and KMS where applicable). URI is stored in the installer run report (local) and optionally emitted to stdout; no credentials are stored. Added a note to docs + scrubbed any accidental full URLs from debug logs.
Connor O'Brien (review): One more: rollback integration should be opt-in, not automatic restore, to avoid surprises.
Devon Price (author): Agreed. Rollback will prompt interactively by default and supports --restore-db-snapshot=<uri> for non-interactive flows; no automatic restore without explicit operator action.
System (CI): integration: backup-postgres failed on first run (docker pull rate limit); rerun succeeded after caching.
Connor O'Brien (final): Approved after last changes.
release_notes: Private installer upgrades now create and verify a control-plane DB snapshot before applying changes (abort-on-failure).
Upgrade summaries/JSON reports include snapshot URI + verification status to support restore drills and faster triage.
Rollback flow can optionally restore a verified pre-upgrade DB snapshot via interactive prompt or flag.
